subject.repo: @nevermined-io/payments 1.13.0 (npm exact pin, unmodified) — express paymentMiddleware, x402 path
subject.sut_note: SUT = published npm dist of the vendor's Express payment middleware, mounted unmodified on a plain Express app (buffered / high-credit / streaming / gateable routes). The facilitator backend behind it is a local HONEST mock whose semantics were modeled one-to-one from the vendor's own published contracts, each decision citing a vendor source line: default mint is v2 (reusable, no nonce; minter resolves (tokenVersion ?? 2) === 3); v3 single-use enforced by a backend nonce store with BCK.X402.0059 on second settle (HTTP 402); verify never consults the nonce and never burns (middleware.ts:1305 comment verbatim); settle may report 200 + success:false (facilitator-api.ts:650). Source audit at repo commit 586ced2a fixed the anchors cited in the findings; the SUT remained the npm dist. Fully offline (Gate D): all traffic on 127.0.0.1, no Nevermined-operated service contacted. Run: 2026-10-27T11:37:08Z, Node v24.22.1, Express 4.21.2, vitest 1.6.1, 11/11 probes executed, suite ~2 s.

scenarios.name: lost-response-retry-double-charge
scenarios.checks: Default v2 token (reusable, no nonce): response #1 produced and settled, buyer never receives it; documented retry re-verifies, handler executes again, settlement burns again. 2 services / 2 settlements for one logical request; no idempotency key, no settlement-query API, and the only reconciliation artifact (payment-response receipt header) is attached to exactly the response that was lost

scenarios.name: single-use-guard-race-and-reactivity
scenarios.checks: P2: two concurrent requests with one fresh v3 token both pass the local spent-map and both verify (verify never consults the nonce), both handlers execute, one settlement burns; the loser is answered 402 after its work. P2b: the success path never marks the token spent locally - the map is armed only by the 0059 error - so the first replay of a successfully settled token re-runs the handler for free before refusal. Guard scope is per-process in-memory; vendor source comment states it does not span horizontally scaled instances and the package provides no shared store

scenarios.name: settle-failure-unpaid-delivery
scenarios.checks: Buffered path withholds the body only for BCK.X402.0059; every other settle failure delivers anyway with a console-only record. P3: hard HTTP 500 -> 2xx delivered, 0 burned; the MPP path routes the equivalent failure through onPaymentError but the x402 path does not. P3b: settle returns the vendor-documented 200 + success:false shape -> middleware never reads success/errorReason, attaches a settlement receipt to a settlement that never happened, delivers the body

scenarios.name: verify-settle-depletion-race
scenarios.checks: Verify checks balance but reserves nothing: two concurrent requests priced at exactly the remaining balance both verify, both handlers run, first settle drains the account, second rejects with BCK.X402.0006 (not the special-cased 0059) and its body is delivered anyway - one paid service and its twin delivered free, deterministically

scenarios.name: streaming-no-receipt
scenarios.checks: Streaming route: headers flush with the first chunk, settlement runs fire-and-forget inside the end wrapper, receipt header is structurally impossible ('headers already flushed; payment-response receipt not attached' - vendor's own stderr). Buyer receives the full value, pays in full, holds nothing naming the transaction; combined with P1 the primary agent endpoint shape cannot reconcile lost-response retries

scenarios.name: silent-v3-downgrade
scenarios.checks: tokenVersion:3 against a pre-v3 backend: the field is dropped without error (whitelist semantics), a reusable v2 token returns. detectAccessTokenVersion reports the true version (good contract, documented), but the downgrade path emits no warning and the default mint is v2 regardless - a buyer who wanted single-use semantics silently holds a reusable credential if they forget to branch

scenarios.name: controls
scenarios.checks: C1 clean buffered v3 purchase: 1 service, 1 settlement, verifiable receipt attached. C3 buyer disconnect before delivery: honestly not charged - the middleware probes actual socket delivery via a byte-delta baseline rather than trusting status codes (handler work wasted remains the seller's cost). C4 empty balance: rejected by verify pre-handler, no delivery, no burn

findings_summary.title: Lost-response retry double-charges on the default v2 token: no idempotency key, no settlement query, receipt attached only to the lost response

Single-use enforcement is per-process and reactive: concurrent race delivers a free service; the guard arms only after witnessing BCK.X402.0059; multi-replica sellers have no guard at all (disclosed in source comment, not in seller-facing docs)

Any settle failure except 0059 delivers the resource unpaid with a console-only record - including the documented 200 + success:false shape, which even receives a settlement receipt; x402 path lacks the onPaymentError notification the MPP path has
Verify does not reserve credits: depletion between verify and settle delivers the second service free (insufficient-credits is not special-cased)
Streamed responses carry no settlement receipt ever (headers flushed) and settle is fire-and-forget after close - reconciliation impossible on the dominant agent endpoint shape
Silent v3->v2 downgrade on mint: SDK detects and returns the true version but emits no warning; default mint is v2 anyway

Confirmed windows: W1 FAIL (High, UNBOUNDED — 402 amount=50000 signed; NO default cap: GatewayClient registers no onBeforePaymentCreation, cap is opt-in only); W2 settle-after-delivery FAIL (High — SETTLEMENT_FAILED throw from pay(); caller retry = new fetch, new sign, new settle: signedPayloads=2, fetchCount=4); W3 retry idempotency FAIL (High — fresh random 32-byte nonce per call, no client-side tracking; both signatures valid 7 days); W4 cross-resource replay FAIL (Medium-High — signed authorization has no resource-URL binding; a signature for resource A reuses for resource B at same payTo+amount within the 7-day window); W5 payTo-binding FAIL (Critical — 402 payTo=0xbaadf00d…0000 signed as to=0xbAadF00D…0000 with no payee check; same surface as SUT-1 W5 / BlockRun F1); W-MCP FAIL (High — two pay() = two payloads + two settlements, no confirmation dialog, no nonce dedup, no idempotency key); W-CAP1 FAIL (High — amount=2000000 ($2.00 vs $0.01 advertised) signed by default; only a user-added hook rejects ('User cap: 100000'); default unsafe); W-CAP2 FAIL (Medium, dust — amount=1 signed silently, no min check); W-VERIFIER FAIL (Critical, Circle-unique — extra.verifyingContract from the 402 response used as the EIP-712 domain with no allowlist: schemeSig over the ATTACKER contract byte-identical to the hand-rolled attacker-domain signature and != real-GatewayWallet signature; the whole signature is misbound, not just payTo — worse than W5); W-MUTATE FAIL (Medium, Circle-unique — ctx.selectedRequirements passed BY REFERENCE: hook mutations of amount ('1') and payTo (attacker) leaked into the signed payload; CF's withX402Client uses structuredClone, Circle does not). Fixation 2026-10-30T13:09:00Z.

findings_summary.title: Critical — payTo-binding missing (SUT-1 CF, SUT-2 Circle): the client signs the payment authorization over an attacker-controlled payTo from the 402 response without any check against the expected recipient — funds rerouting on-chain; same surface as BlockRun F1 (argus-seal-0006). CDP ships the fix shape (allowedPayees) but only as an opt-in guardrail.

Critical — verifyingContract misbinding (SUT-2 Circle-unique): extra.verifyingContract from the 402 response becomes the EIP-712 domain with no allowlist; the whole signature is bound to an attacker-supplied contract (verified byte-identical against a hand-rolled attacker-domain signature and != the real-GatewayWallet signature) — strictly worse than payTo-only substitution.

Silent double-charge on paid tool calls (SUT-1 CF, SUT-2 Circle; inherited via the shared x402Client in SUT-3): no confirmation callback by default, no idempotency key, no nonce dedup — retry / double-click / eviction recovery re-signs and re-settles for one logical operation.

Amount/quote binding missing; default-cap posture uneven (W1 + W-CAP1): server-declared 402 amounts are signed without binding to the advertised price — CF bounded by its $0.10 default cap, Circle unbounded (no default cap, opt-in only), CdpX402Client removes the upstream $1 default cap (F-WNOCONTROLS); with W-CAP2 both directions of amount mismatch are unguarded by default.

Settle-after-delivery double execution (SUT-1 CF, SUT-2 Circle): SETTLEMENT_FAILED surfaces as a fresh 402-with-accepts (CF) or a throw -> caller retry (both) — a lost settle response yields a second full round (verify/settle/exec x2) with no recovery handles and no idempotency.

Retry idempotency absent (SUT-1 CF, SUT-2 Circle): every retry mints a fresh nonce with no client-side tracking or dedup; SUT-2 signatures stay valid for the full 7-day validity window — dedup is left entirely to the gateway.

Signed token not bound to its target (SUT-1 CF: cross-tool same-price replay — token matched by scheme/network/price only; SUT-2 Circle: no resource-URL binding, 7-day window): a signature issued for one tool/resource is accepted for another.
No minimum-amount check (all three SUTs): dust amounts (1 atomic = $0.000001 vs $0.01 advertised) are signed silently — combined with W1/W-CAP1 the whole amount range is unguarded by default.

Hook mutation leaks into the signed payload (SUT-2 Circle-unique): ctx.selectedRequirements is passed by reference, so confirmation-hook mutations of amount/payTo reach the signed authorization; CF's structuredClone defense (NEG2 control) shows the correct pattern.

findings_summary.title: Result: the shipped @x402-lens/express middleware satisfies the whole lab battery with ZERO defects — 18 PASS / 3 DOCUMENTED / 0 FAIL across 21 sealed sessions. Canonical gate green end-to-end (402 → pay → verify → settle → deliver with the full event stream); no delivery without a valid payment in any fault session (undecodable payload, verify rejection, facilitator 500/timeout); upfront flow: failing settle never calls the handler (documented guarantee holds); authorization-flow settle failure matches the documented trade-off AND still emits payment.settle_failed; identical PAYMENT-SIGNATURE resubmission is refused at the second verify (honest facilitator, duplicate_payment_nonce) — exactly one delivery, zero new signer calls; grant bypass is never silent (access.granted/access.denied always emitted); a throwing sink never breaks a payment; the wire form is untouched (observer read-only); config surface refuses exactly the documented shapes and accepts the valid multi-network control; shipped CLI gates healthy against the live SUT. Verdicts are claims about the CANDIDATE (with its documented carve-outs) vs the lab battery, not about the x402 protocol or the @x402 SDK baseline.

Observations (nuances, NOT defects; both fail closed): (1) runtime payment.settle_failed events carry the facilitator reason verbatim but findings: [] — the SDK settle error does not expose the structured settle response under the keys the lens's settleFromError reads (settleResponse/result/body), so settlement_pending / settlement_failed findings render only via `x402-lens explain --settle` (engine rule checkSettlementVerdict is correct; the CLI snapshot test pins it). Non-terminal semantics (reason carried, reconcile-not-retry advice, no delivery claim) hold at runtime. (2) a flat facilitatorHeaders object is rejected by the SDK exactly as documented (D-17) — no facilitator contact, no delivery, process survives — but the rejection surfaces as HTTP 500 on the first payment request rather than a config-time refusal; the lens SOURCE comment promises early validation ('validated once here rather than surfacing as a failed payment later') while the README makes no such promise. Cosmetic robustness gap.

Methodology note (honesty discipline): the first full battery run produced 11 non-PASS sessions; a per-session fact review attributed ALL of them to lab equipment, not to the candidate — 8 matcher bugs (empty handler dict compared as !== 0), 1 replay-capture race in the lab client (replay slots started before the slot-1 header capture), 1 mislocated expectation (flat facilitatorHeaders is rejected by the SDK at request time, not at config resolution — the probe was moved to an honest HTTP session), 1 unaccounted documented CLI behavior (inspect exits 1 with the CORS readiness report on a cors-off server). Matchers/harness fixed, sessions re-run clean: 21/21. Raw first-run ledgers stay lab-local (not committed); the second-run fixture and per-session facts are the sealed evidence.

records.summary: Independent probe 2026-11-21 (~03:44-04:05 UTC). Zero settled paid calls (sandbox burner unfunded: Base mainnet native 0, USDC 0), budget regulation <=$0.01 kept at $0.00. Findings. (1) Transport passport: initialize -> protocolVersion 2025-06-18 accepted, stateless (no Mcp-Session-Id header); tools/list free on lite (search_tools + call_tool) and full endpoint (1020 tools in one 1.79MB page, no cursor); full catalog snapshot + docs-all snapshot in evidence. (2) Challenge semantics: calling a paid tool without payment returns MCP result isError=true whose text is the x402 v2 PaymentRequired JSON (x402Version 2, error 'Payment required', resource.url = the MCP endpoint itself, extensions.bazaar with toolName/inputSchema discovery metadata, accepts[] with the two network options) — HTTP status stays 200; the plain-HTTPS path documented in the README uses HTTP 402 + PAYMENT-REQUIRED header instead. (3) Gate order: payment gate precedes argument validation — call_tool(url_parse, {url:12345}) and call_tool(cusip_validate, {cusip:'!!!not-a-cusip!!!'}) both return the same PaymentRequired challenge instead of a validation error, so an agent cannot learn its arguments are wrong without paying; unknown tool name returns RPC -32602 'Unknown tool' for free (MCP layer validates tool existence before the gate). (4) Signed submit: x402 v2 payload {x402Version, resource, accepted, payload:{authorization, signature}} built from the challenge (EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization, value=1000, validAfter/validBefore from maxTimeoutSeconds 300, nonce random) signed with a burner EOA over the challenge-supplied domain (USD Coin v2, chainId 8453, verifyingContract USDC) and submitted in params._meta['x402/payment'] -> server forwarded to the facilitator: verify returned invalid_exact_evm_insufficient_balance in 1.04s — the signature was VALID (not invalid_signature), the failure is the balance check, i.e. the payload shape and EIP-712 domain are correct end-to-end; the failed verify response carries the full fresh challenge (same accepts, new terms) so the client can retry after funding. No settle transaction, no charge; burner balance 0/0 before and after (evidence 21). (5) 'If the tool fails, you're not charged': pre-payment failures are free by construction (no payment token in the request); the post-payment refund/settle-on-failure path requires a funded wallet and is UNVERIFIED in this run — the observable equivalent is that no settle ever occurred without a valid payment (facilitator balance-gates before settle).
